ROOT_CAUSE: The fourth NAME pattern (`\n\s*-\s*([A-Z][a-zà-öø-ÿ]+(?:\s+[A-Z][a-zà-öø-ÿ]+)?)\b`) incorrectly matches the verb phrase "talking about" after "I'm", while failing to match multi-word names with special characters like accented letters or hyphens (e.g., 'Rosa-Maria', 'Emilia Cervántez') because it restricts characters to uppercase/lowercase ASCII/accented ranges without punctuation or lowercase support.
RULE: All NAME regex patterns must explicitly anchor full names with proper character classes (including hyphens and lowercase support) and avoid overly broad prepositional or verb phrase matches like "I'm [verb/adverb]".
NEXT_EDIT: Fix the signature dash pattern and third-party relationship patterns to correctly capture multi-word names with hyphens and accented characters while tightening the intro pattern to exclude verb phrases like 'talking about'.
